Journal 1:

My goal for today is to draw up the schematic and layout the pcb.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sCBI3ojvDWBP38LVSmrM83tqWftTfcqi/3cf3d0690971e83eb0c688634661f906534da00203be3701809d2b66c6f27826.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sCBI3ojvDWBP38LVSmrM83tqWftTfcqi/6fc0ae0f112144a38a891b8abc14b5274ef9ec7abe3378954ebf90d1038ee629.png)

I went with the rp2040 for some weird reason so i had to route my usb c, my flash memory, my quartz clock and just all in all suffer. By some miracle I managed to wire it all but i looked at it and thought, im not soldering all that, so now i need to look for alternatives so ctrl-a and delete, back to the drawing board. Thats how i landed on the pi pico, which will save me all the pain of wiring and soldering flash memory or quartz clocks, now all i needed to do was add my buttons.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sCBI3ojvDWBP38LVSmrM83tqWftTfcqi/d93b19f449b93b6ac6658ffd0be4085fa79ccb6916b33694944f7c93fd897d86.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sCBI3ojvDWBP38LVSmrM83tqWftTfcqi/4d65537d7f9392eb56dfc9ecc168c08abf7dc64d55eeb7257d63271fdc5e5572.png)
I use 6 buttons, 4 are “performance” buttons, they are the buttons that will play the sound effects or the set beats, the remaining 2 are used as “pagers” they will be able to page between what the performance buttons are set to, so effectively i can have lets say, 16 buttons while only needing to use 4.

I also added a copper filling around the pcb, to reduce noise and interference.

### 2026-10-21 – Journal 2:

**6.8h**

Journal 2:
My goal for today was to write some code and bring this 8-button controller to life.
Started out writing a MicroPython. Since all 8 buttons use pull-ups and share a ground rail, I mapped them across GPIO 0 to 7. Added a 15ms software debounce check because tactile buttons usually chatter when you click them, which would otherwise spam your DAW with a million accidental MIDI notes.
I made the firmware a multi-page system using a page-switcher button. Instead of just triggers, I split it into 4 pages using the 4 performance pads:
Page 0: Drums (standard MIDI map for kicks, snares, hats)
Page 1: samples
Page 2: A 4-Track Looper
Page 3: A synth/piano mode for playing melodic leads
The looper page took some time to get right. Each of the 4 pads controls an independent loop track. You give it a short press to start recording, short-press again to lock it in and switch to playback, and a long press (> 1 second) to delete the loop. Imo the coolest part is cross-page recording: you can start recording a loop track on the looper page, switch over to the drums page to play drums (ig), and it captures the notes into your loop.
total time: 6.8 hours
